posts.content_md:
Don't know how to say this, so I'll just dive right in -- this is not really about holography, but about an arts project I have in mind where I need a transparent dye or pigmet (to the visible) that fluoresces at a given wavelength. I actually need several of the dye/pigmants that will fluoresce at several different wavelengths. What I want to do is to multiply fluoresce compounds via strobe of different uv or ir wavelengths inside a "hall of mirrors" effect (mirror and half-silvered surface, topcoated to prevent uv/ir transmission, eg). I found a company called nanoptics, but they no longet make the dyes. They mentioned 3-HF and HBT, and suggested I look at manufacturers of laser dyes.

I thought I'd post here on the off chance anyone understands what I'm trying to do and is able to help. Thanks.
